feedback.problem:
Let $y={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n}$ be a series solution to the equation $4{y}^{′}-y=0.$ 

What is the recurrence relation for the coefficients ${a}_{n},$ where $n=0,1,2…?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find ${y}^{′}(x)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & ={({\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & ={({a}_{0}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n})}^{′} \\  & =0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute expressions for $y(x)$ and ${y}^{′}(x)$ into the given differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }n{a}_{n}{x}^{n-1}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We want to make the powers of $x$ the same. Therefore, in the first sum, we change the index of the summation by writing $m=n-1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\sum }_{m=0}^{\infty }(m+1){a}_{m+1}{x}^{m}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $m$ with $n$ in the first summation (since it does not matter which letter we use) gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }(n+1){a}_{n+1}{x}^{n}-{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{n} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since both sums now start with $n=0,$ we can combine them as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }[4(n+1){a}_{n+1}-{a}_{n}]{x}^{n} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Setting each coefficient of $x$ equal to zero, we obtain

$$
4(n+1){a}_{n+1}-{a}_{n}=0.
$$

Finally, the recursion formula is

$$
{a}_{n+1}=\frac{{a}_{n}}{4(n+1)},\,n=0,1,2….
$$
